{{Quote|Tour the Desert Planet Bar Neth|Advertisement on the Tourscan|<ref name="ST" />}}
'''Bar Neth''' (also spelled '''Bar-Neth''') was a former [[Desert/Legends|desert]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located in the [[Bar Neth system/Legends|Bar Neth system]], a quinary [[Star system/Legends|star system]] positioned in the [[Albarrio sector/Legends|Albarrio sector]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. By the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[4 ABY/Legends|4.3 ABY]], Bar Neth had been turned into a "Natural Wonderland" with bountiful farmlands. As a result of its ambitious [[Terraforming/Legends|terraforming]] process, Bar Neth was considered pleasant to live in and was hugely apealing for galactic tourists. At that [[Time/Legends|time]], trips to Bar Neth were organized by the [[Star Tours/Legends|Star Tours]] travel agency as part of their [[Frontier Vacation Package]].

==Description==
{{Quote|A Natural Wonderland|Advertisement on the Tourscan|<ref name="ST" />}}
[[File:Bar-Neth_fields_Epcot.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Vast fields of crops were planted on Bar Neth]]
Bar Neth was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="ST" /> located in the [[Bar Neth system/Legends|Bar Neth system]],<ref name="EAOC" /> a quinary<ref name="ST" /> [[Star system/Legends|star system]] positioned in the [[Albarrio sector/Legends|Albarrio sector]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="EAOC" /> Its landscape consisted of wide, ochre-[[Color/Legends|colored]] cliffs, bluffs and canyons. However, following an ambitious desert reclamation process, [[Plant/Legends|flora]] was introduced in the planet's environment.<ref name="ST" />

Subsequently, nature reclaimed its rights over the planet's ecosystem. Many wild [[Cactus/Legends|cacti]] grew on Bar Neth, and vast groves of cultivated [[Fruit/Legends|fruits]] spread throughout the land, overflown by harvesting machines and airborne lifters. Occasional round desert houses were also scattered across the planet's surface. In its [[Terraforming/Legends|terraformed]] state, Bar Neth was regarded as a "Natural Wonderland" and an attractive place to live in. The climate on Bar Neth remained hot, with temperatures as high as 38° centigrade.<ref name="ST" /> Even after its terraforming, Bar Neth's surface was also subject to local [[Sandstorm/Legends|dust storms]], which could reduce visibility to at least two [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]].<ref name="ST" />

==History==
{{Quote|Campings & Safaris<br />Zero-Gravity Golf Courses|Advertisement on the Tourscan|<ref name="ST" />}}
[[File:Bar-Neth_Epcot.jpg|thumb|250px|The surface of the terraformed Bar Neth]]
Originally, Bar Neth was a complete wasteland devoid of lifeforms. However, at some point before the rise of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], a massive arid-zone agriculture project was launched, and a vast number of [[Labor droid/Legends|labor droids]] worked hard to change Bar Neth into a green planet with lush vegetation. As a result of the new flora and relaxing environment, Bar Neth became one of the most popular family resorts in the galaxy. Popular stops and activities on the planet included the [[Carl Hodgesville Dude Ranch]], various camping and safaris sites, and a zero-[[Gravity/Legends|gravity]] [[golf]] course.<ref name="ST" />

By the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[4 ABY/Legends|4.3 ABY]],<ref name="LC blog">{{Blog|holocron|7|Death Star timeline}}</ref> the [[Star Tours/Legends|Star Tours]] interplanetary travel agency organized trips to Bar Neth as a part of its [[Frontier Vacation Package]]. That package was notably advertised in the company's [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceports]] through a video display device known as the "[[Tourscan]]," for which the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] announcer [[Dan Android]] would provide narration.<ref name="ST" />

==Behind the scenes==
Bar Neth was introduced in the Tourscan by Dan Android at the [[Tokyo Disneyland]] [[Star Tours (real-world)|''Star Tours'']].<ref name="ST" /> The location and footage was in actually recycled from one of the locations from the now-defunct [[Wikipedia:Epcot|Epcot]] dark ride attraction [[Wikipedia:Horizons (Epcot)|Horizons]], specifically the [[Wikipedia:Mesa Verde National Park|Mesa Verde]] ending segment of the ride. Mesa Verde, the segment of Horizons that the clip originated from, focused on the concept of [[Wikipedia:Arid-zone agriculture|arid-zone agriculture]], even going as far as to give a smell of fresh [[Wikipedia:Orange|oranges]] at one segment of the ride.<ref name="Epcot">{{WebCite|url=http://progresscityusa.com/2011/09/01/the-horizons-story-part-iii-disneys-house-of-magic|text=The Horizons Story, Part III: Disney's House Of Magic|author=Michael Crawford|date=2011-09-24|work=The Horizons Story|archivedate=20110924203238}}</ref>

The models for the three ending segments of Horizons were designed, constructed and filmed by none other than [[David Jones]], a special-effects veteran of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]. According to Jones, the desert film involved an 86-foot model and was the longest continuous sequence ever done with miniatures.<ref name="Epcot" /> In addition, to save up on the budget, the set only had one house developed. In the original Horizons ride, the plant groves being harvested were laorange trees, also known as long orange trees.<ref name="Horizons Pavilion">{{WebCite|url=http://www.kesigndesign.com/code/horizon1.shtml|text=Choose Your Tomorrow attraction, Horizon Pavilion, EPCOT, Walt Disney World Visual Effects - Model and Prop Builder and Special Effects.|author=Kenneth A. Larson|archivedate=20140327071735}}</ref>

The ''Star Tours'' attraction mentioned the "Carl Hodgesville Dude Ranch,"<ref name="ST" /> which was named after [[Wikipedia:Carl Hodges|Carl Hodges]], director of the Environmental Research Lab at the [[Wikipedia:University of Arizona|University of Arizona]]. He helped the team working on the Mesa Verde segment create a futuristic, yet plausible, environment.<ref name="Epcot" /> Hodges' research aim at creating vast saltwater irrigated farms along the world's desert coasts.<ref name="VF">{{WebCite|url=http://www.vanityfair.com/news/2007/04/hodges200704|text=The Future's Farmer|work=Vanity Fair|archivedate=20160713074719}}</ref>

Although the name of the planet was spelled both as "Bar Neth" and "Bar-Neth" on different screens of the Tourscan, Lucasfilm specifically requested that the unhyphenated version be used in [[Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion|''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion]].<ref name="Twitter Jfry">{{Twitter|jasoncfry|status/636656092685070336|[[Jason Fry]]|quote=@LelalMekha I don't know your policies for such things, but LFL's intent is that "Bar Neth" is canonical (within Legends).|archivefile=File:Bar_Neth_tweet.png}}</ref>
